newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thaksin, Virabongsa brought into cabinet. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh decided late last night to bring economist Virabongsa Ramangkura and telecom tycoon Thaksin Shinawatra into his cabinet.

- Security guard key to solving car-park blast. Police believe that a security guard who lost his right hand and several toes on his left foot in an explosion in the car park of a Phaholyothin Road building yesterday holds the key to solving the crime.

Boonley Lapham, 30, who is in a critical condition in Phaya Thai II Hospital, was the only victim of the blast which damanged nine parked cars and triggered an evacuation of the building, which houses the local branch of the American company IBM. (THE NATION)

- Ucom resorts to slash in salaries. The economic crisis has forced United Communication Industry Plc, one of the country's largest telecom groups, to cut the salaries of its 4,000 employees starting next month, according to the company's chairman.

Shibhumi Sukhanetr, Ucom Group chairman, told The Nation the group last Friday announced reductions in payroll payments by cutting 7.5 per cent off the salaries of those in low to middle positions, 10 per cent off managers, 15 per cent off senior management executives' salaries. (THE NATION BUSINESS)

- VAT revenue may fall short of target. The increase in value added tax (VAT) from 7 per cent to 10 per cent may not help bolster the government's revenue to meet International Monetary Fund (IMF) stipulations for standby credit as originally hoped.
The government told the IMF that the VAT increase would generate extra revenue of 66 billion baht. (BANGKOK POST)
